author: root/coordinator

checks.description: The default diagnostic remains writer-free; only explicit commissioning composition embeds the target writer and policy in content protected by the SD-resident verified-initrd hash chain.

The trusted initramfs executes the embedded writer before switching to network-root code, mounts NFS read-only only as the exact image source, and passes bounded commissioning and claim-port parameters.
A local explicit host controller prepares a short-lived exact-image job and durable one-shot claim, signs only after durable consumption, and fails closed without automatic retry or rearm.

Synthetic QEMU passes end-to-end success, source/identity/job/claim refusal, replay/lost acknowledgement, interruption, flush/readback faults and unchanged diagnostic checks using disposable media only.

Strict builds, focused tests and hash-bound evidence pass; documentation explicitly excludes SoC secure boot, live CID/dev_t, physical write/power-loss behavior and release qualification. H12 remains the only physical gate.

constraints.text: Implement only the SD route under this approval. Keep the ordinary diagnostic writer-free. Report the SD hash chain as protection against changed payloads on the card in owner custody, not as SoC-rooted authentication of the physical card.

Keep the writer, target policy, job, signatures and claim verifier in the SD-resident initramfs as the running root. Require the exact read-only NFS image mount and reject an absent, wrong or writable mount before target open. Never execute network-supplied code. Preserve terminal refusal after an uncertain or post-open failure.

Bind the manually started controller to the audited v5 image/map and one local target policy. Enforce private-input ownership and modes, bounded validity, durable claim consumption before signing, and no automatic retry or rearm. Measure the composed SD/initramfs and host scratch requirements against the existing limits.

Test and document what happens on the next boot with the SD card still installed after success, refusal and interruption. Do not claim the owner's no-human-action-per-write objective is met unless an independently reviewed unattended entry and return path demonstrates it; retain fail-closed behavior meanwhile.

Keep all acceptance evidence offline and synthetic. H12 still requires fresh live CID/dev_t comparison, exact artifact and recovery review, an immediate separate high-consequence review, and explicit authorization before a physical write.

decision.rationale: Select the SD trusted-initramfs route as the single primary route for this bounded offline feature. The 2026-09-26 H09/H10 records show that the identified printer booted the SD kernel and initramfs, reached read-only NFS, and exposed the installed eMMC for reads. The 2026-09-27 kexec assessment finds CONFIG_KEXEC disabled in the physically booted v5 kernel and no tested H616 handoff. The current SD builder instead runs init from NFS, so it cannot safely launch the writer; the H616 candidate is explicitly nonbootable. Moving the reviewed writer and policy into the SD-resident initramfs addresses that gap while retaining the synthetic-only evidence boundary. SD custody matters because the SoC has no established secure-boot root: hashes stored on the same replaceable card do not authenticate a substituted card. This approval covers offline composition and tests, not an unattended physical write, boot-policy change, H12 authorization, or release. It also does not establish that leaving the SD card installed permits normal eMMC boot after a terminal writer result.

evidence.limitations: Offline composition only. No physical H616 boot, live target identity, eMMC write or boot-policy change; SD custody is not SoC secure boot.
evidence.method: Inspected default and explicit boot scripts; built synthetic H616 bundle and repacked pinned diagnostic initramfs, then extracted writer and PID 1 ORDER. Repeated same inputs and matched SHA-256. Ran 47 focused and regression tests in a clean offline worktree.

evidence.limitations: Mount admission and fallback are synthetic/static checks. No live NFS or physical boot; end-to-end QEMU and power-loss behavior remain later tasks.
evidence.method: Verified commissioning bootargs force root=/dev/ram0 and boot=nfs, so kernel fallback cannot execute NFS init. Checked pinned initramfs PID 1 sources ORDER; compiled mount parser self-test for exact read-only NFS export and tested wrong/missing/writable/duplicate mounts. Ran 47 focused and regression tests.

tasks.resumption: Use root=/dev/ram0 plus boot=nfs for the trusted initramfs mount path; prohibit NFS kernel fallback, retest, and re-review the replacement commit.
tasks.title: Run the writer from authenticated initramfs content

verification.rationale: Reviewed the complete five-file diff from 5dc8ce9 to clean HEAD 0ff91b6. The default diagnostic remains writer-free. Explicit commissioning places the writer and policy inputs in the SD-hash-verified initramfs. Its boot arguments use root=/dev/ram0 with boot=nfs: initramfs-tools still mounts the specified NFS source read-only at /root, while failure of /init cannot make the kernel execute an NFS-supplied init. The sourced init-bottom ORDER execs the embedded writer before run-init; writer admission checks the exact mount, read-only flags, bundle and claim before target open. Verified all submitted document and source hashes, proposal and requirement hashes, and the reported twb-01/twb-02 offline scope. The 47 reported tests were not rerun in this read-only session. No physical boot, eMMC write or release behavior is certified.
